voiceover: Almost any story about Jesus starts where a life starts — a birth, a family tree, a river baptism. The Gospel of John starts before the beginning of anything at all. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Who is the Word? A few lines later John tells us: the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. The Word is Jesus of Nazareth. First, notice the verb. Of created things, John uses a verb that means came to be. Of the Word, he says: was. When the beginning happened, the Word already was. Second: the Word was with God. John sets two claims side by side, not collapsed into one. The Word is personally distinct from the Father — not another name for him. Third: the Word was God. And two verses later John says: all things were made through him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. So the Word is not among the things made. He stands on the Maker's side of the line between Creator and creation. So John holds two truths together. Distinct from the Father. And fully sharing the one divine nature. Not one traded away for the other. And the theme runs all through John's Gospel. Jesus prays: Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory that I had with you before the world existed. And when Thomas sees the risen Jesus, he answers him: My Lord and my God — and Jesus receives it. In the beginning was the Word. The Word was God. And that Word became flesh, and lived among us.
